newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to call confidence vote on milk bill.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to call confidence vote on milk bill.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government said on Tuesday it would call a vote of confidence in the upper house of parliament (Senate) to ram a decree to reform the milk sector into law.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi, whose coalition commands a clear majority in the Senate, won a similar do-or-die motion in the lower house last week.
The vote was expected to be held on Wednesday, political sources said.

The decree was hastily introduced after farmers blockaded roads and airports across northern Italy in January to protest against strict European Union dairy quotas and tough fines for overproduction of milk.

The bill offers cheap loans and payments by instalment plus a pledge by the government to set up a commission to examine the farmers' grievances. Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas.

Decree laws issued by the government have force for only 60 days unless approved within that time by parliament. They cannot be re-issued and Prodi has called several confidence votes to push through legislation. He has survived them all comfortably. The milk decree expires on April 1.
